content.text:
Queued prompts can now be edited, and the send menu has a new "Queue" option. All 215 tests pass (1 ignored), the build has no warnings, and `piton check`, `piton build check` and `piton build` pass. I haven't tried either feature in the app.

**Editing a queued prompt:**
- **Edit button:** each prompt in the queue list has a pencil button next to its cancel button. It's disabled while that prompt is still being saved, and the row stays highlighted while you edit it.
- **In the chat input:** clicking the pencil sets your current draft (text, attachments, tab) aside and loads the queued prompt with its own attachments and mode. You get full completions and language support while editing.
  - **Status row:** a row above the input reads "Editing queued prompt 2" with "Ctrl+Enter to save · Esc to cancel", and the send button reads "Save". The send menu is unavailable while editing.
  - **Save or cancel:** Ctrl+Enter or Save writes the edit, Esc cancels, and either way your set-aside draft comes back exactly as it was.
- **Held while editing:** a prompt being edited is never sent, even by auto-send or "Send next". Anything queued behind it waits. Once the edit is saved or cancelled, the queue carries on.
- **Saving:** the edited text goes back into the same queue position, in the same file on disk. If it can't be saved, the prompt stays as it was and a "Could not save the queued prompt" notification says why.
- **Interruptions:** clicking edit on another prompt moves your editing to that one. Cancelling the prompt from the list, or switching projects, cancels the edit.

**"Queue" option:** it's the menu's second option.
- **Queues without sending:** it adds the prompt to the queue and clears the input, even when the harness is free. It then waits: it goes when you click "Send next", or when the next task finishes with auto-send on.
- **Ask tab:** the option is disabled there, and the arrow keys skip over it, since questions never queue.

**Spec:** the Prompt Editor's queue section covers editing and queueing a prompt deliberately. The Chat Input scope covers the new menu option and the editing state.

**Tests:**
- **Chat input:** covers the Queue option through the keyboard and being skipped on the Ask tab. It also covers editing: the set-aside draft, Esc cancel, Ctrl+Enter save, and the menu staying closed while editing.
- **Prompt view:** a queued prompt is held while edited, and switching to edit a second prompt works. The edit is saved back in place on disk, and a deliberately queued prompt isn't sent while the harness is free.
- **Queue storage:** an edited prompt keeps its position.

My first version of the prompt-view test gave its temporary project an empty config. Saving failed there, because filling in the system prompt needs the spec and code locations, and the test caught it. I then gave that project a real config.
